course.title: Welding and Metalwork
course.tagline: Cut, join and shape metal into gates, frames and furniture.

days.title: Welding Safety: Gear Up
days.goal: Know the safety gear and rules before you strike an arc.
steps: Wear a welding helmet, gloves, long sleeves and boots.
Learn that the arc (the bright light) can burn eyes and skin.
Work in fresh air: welding smoke is harmful to breathe.
Keep water and a fire extinguisher close.
days.task: Put on full safety gear and check every item.
days.challenge: Name every piece of safety gear and what it protects.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to put on before welding?
options: Full safety gear: helmet, gloves, long sleeves, boots
quiz.explain: Full gear protects eyes, skin and feet from arc light, sparks and hot metal.

quiz.q: Why is welding smoke dangerous?
options: It is harmful to breathe and needs fresh air
quiz.explain: Welding fumes carry metal particles that harm lungs, so work in fresh air.

quiz.q: What is the arc in welding?
options: The bright light and heat that melts the metal
quiz.explain: The arc is the electric spark that melts metal so pieces join.

days.title: Welding Tools and Metals
days.goal: Know the welder, rods and the metals you will join.
steps: Learn the parts: the welder, the electrode holder and the earth clamp.
A welding rod (electrode) is the stick that melts to join metal.
Feel mild steel, the easiest metal for beginners.
Set up a clean metal workbench.
days.task: Label the parts of a welder: holder, clamp and dials.
days.challenge: Tell mild steel from aluminium by look and weight.

quiz.q: What are the parts of a welder?
options: The welder, the electrode holder and the earth clamp.
quiz.explain: Learn the parts: the welder, the electrode holder and the earth clamp.

quiz.q: What is a welding rod?
options: The stick that melts to join metal.
quiz.explain: A welding rod (electrode) is the stick that melts to join metal.

quiz.q: Which metal is easiest for beginners?
quiz.explain: Feel mild steel, the easiest metal for beginners.

days.title: Strike Your First Arc
days.goal: Strike an arc and hold it steady on scrap metal.
steps: Clamp the earth lead to your metal piece.
Tap the rod on the metal like striking a match to start the arc.
Hold the rod a few millimetres from the metal to keep the arc alive.
Practise striking the arc ten times in a row.
days.task: Strike and hold an arc for five seconds on scrap.
days.challenge: Strike the arc first try, five times in a row.

quiz.q: What should you clamp to your metal piece before you strike an arc?
quiz.explain: Clamp the earth lead to your metal piece.

quiz.q: How do you start an arc?
options: Tap the rod on the metal like striking a match.
quiz.explain: Tap the rod on the metal like striking a match to start the arc.

quiz.q: What is the arc in welding?
options: The bright light and heat that melts the metal
quiz.explain: The arc is the electric spark that melts metal so pieces join.

days.title: Stick Welding Basics
days.goal: Run your first straight weld beads on flat metal.
steps: A weld bead is the line of melted metal that joins two pieces.
Move the rod slowly and steadily along the joint.
Keep the same angle and distance the whole way.
Let the bead cool, then chip off the slag (the crust on top).
days.task: Run three straight beads on flat metal.
days.challenge: Run a bead that is straight and even from end to end.

quiz.q: What is a welding rod?
options: The stick that melts to join metal
quiz.explain: The rod (electrode) melts into the joint to form the weld.

quiz.q: What is a weld bead?
options: The line of melted metal that joins two pieces
quiz.explain: The bead is the raised line of metal left after welding.

quiz.q: What is slag?
options: The crust that forms on top of a stick weld
quiz.explain: Slag is the crust that covers a stick weld and must be chipped off.

days.title: Weld Beads: Straight and Even
days.goal: Practise beads until they are straight, even and strong.
steps: Watch the molten pool (the glowing liquid metal) and follow it.
Move at a steady speed: too fast makes a thin bead, too slow makes a fat one.
Keep the rod angle the same.
Compare your beads and keep the best one.
days.task: Run five beads and pick the straightest one.
days.challenge: Run a bead with no gaps or holes in it.

quiz.q: What should you watch as you weld a bead?
options: The molten pool, the glowing liquid metal.
quiz.explain: Watch the molten pool (the glowing liquid metal) and follow it.

quiz.q: What is a weld bead?
options: The line of melted metal that joins two pieces
quiz.explain: The bead is the raised line of metal left after welding.

quiz.q: What happens if you move the rod too slow?
quiz.explain: Move at a steady speed: too fast makes a thin bead, too slow makes a fat one.

days.title: Join Two Pieces: Butt Joint
days.goal: Weld two flat pieces edge to edge.
steps: Line the two pieces up with a tiny gap between them.
Tack weld (small spot welds) at both ends to hold them.
Run a bead along the whole joint.
Check the back: the weld should show through.
days.task: Weld two plates edge to edge so they hold firm.
days.challenge: Weld a butt joint that does not break when bent.

quiz.q: How should you line up two pieces for a butt joint?
options: With a tiny gap between them.
quiz.explain: Line the two pieces up with a tiny gap between them.

quiz.q: What is a weld bead?
options: The line of melted metal that joins two pieces
quiz.explain: The bead is the raised line of metal left after welding.

quiz.q: How do you know a butt joint weld went through?
options: The weld shows through on the back.
quiz.explain: Check the back: the weld should show through.

days.title: Project: Run Weld Beads on a Practice Plate
days.goal: Fill a practice plate with neat parallel beads.

video.title: How to Strike an Arc: Stick Welding Basics

steps: Clean the plate and clamp it flat.
Run beads in straight parallel lines across the plate.
Keep each bead the same width and spacing.
Chip the slag and inspect every bead.
days.task: Finish a plate covered in neat, even beads.
days.challenge: Fill the plate with beads that are all the same width.

quiz.q: What should you do to the plate before you run beads on it?
options: Clean it and clamp it flat.
quiz.explain: Clean the plate and clamp it flat.

quiz.q: How should the beads on the practice plate look?
options: Straight, parallel, the same width and spacing.
quiz.explain: Run beads in straight parallel lines across the plate. Keep each bead the same width and spacing.

quiz.q: What happens if you move the rod too fast?
options: The bead is thin and weak
quiz.explain: Moving too fast leaves too little metal, so the bead is thin and weak.

project.title: Run Weld Beads on a Practice Plate
project.brief: Fill a practice plate with neat parallel weld beads.

days.title: Tack Welding
days.goal: Use tack welds to hold pieces in place before the full weld.

video.title: How to Strike an Arc: Stick Welding Basics

steps: A tack weld is a small quick weld that holds parts together.
Tack at the ends and the middle of a joint.
Check the pieces are square before you tack.
Tack, check, then weld fully.
days.task: Tack a frame square before welding it fully.
days.challenge: Tack a frame so it stays square after welding.

quiz.q: What is a tack weld?
options: A small quick weld that holds parts together.
A full weld along the whole joint.
quiz.explain: A tack weld is a small quick weld that holds parts together.

quiz.q: Where should you tack a joint?
options: At the ends and the middle.
quiz.explain: Tack at the ends and the middle of a joint.

quiz.q: What should you check before you tack?
quiz.explain: Check the pieces are square before you tack.

days.title: Weld a Corner Joint
days.goal: Weld two pieces at a right angle.

video.title: How to Strike an Arc: Stick Welding Basics

steps: Set the pieces at 90 degrees and clamp them.
Tack both ends, then check the angle with a square.
Run a bead along the inside corner.
Check the joint is strong and square.
days.task: Weld a corner joint that is square and strong.
days.challenge: Weld a corner with no gaps at the ends.

quiz.q: How should you set two pieces for a corner joint?
quiz.explain: Set the pieces at 90 degrees and clamp them.

quiz.q: What should you check with a square after tacking a corner?
quiz.explain: Tack both ends, then check the angle with a square.

quiz.q: Where do you run the bead on a corner joint?
quiz.explain: Run a bead along the inside corner.

days.title: Stick Welding (SMAW) 101
days.goal: Understand stick welding: rods, current and settings.
steps: SMAW is the full name for stick welding.
Learn that thicker rods need more current (power).
Set the welder to the right amps for your rod size.
Practise with the settings from the rod box.
days.task: Set a welder to the right amps for a rod size.
days.challenge: Explain what SMAW means in plain words.

quiz.q: What does SMAW stand for?
options: Shielded Metal Arc Welding, the full name for stick welding
quiz.explain: SMAW is stick welding: a rod shielded by its own coating.

quiz.q: What happens if the current is too high?
options: It burns holes in the metal
quiz.explain: Too much current melts through thin metal and leaves holes.

quiz.q: Why test settings on scrap first?
options: So the real piece is welded with the right settings
quiz.explain: Scrap lets you dial in the settings before touching the real work.

days.title: Rod Sizes and Current
days.goal: Pick the right rod and current for the metal thickness.
steps: Thin metal needs a thin rod and low current.
Thick metal needs a thick rod and higher current.
Too much current burns holes; too little makes a weak weld.
Test on scrap before you weld the real piece.
days.task: Pick the right rod and amps for three metal thicknesses.
days.challenge: Weld thin metal without burning a hole in it.

quiz.q: What should thin metal be welded with?
options: A thin rod and low current.
A thick rod and high current.
quiz.explain: Thin metal needs a thin rod and low current.

quiz.q: What happens if the current is too high?
options: It burns holes in the metal
quiz.explain: Too much current melts through thin metal and leaves holes.

quiz.q: Why test settings on scrap first?
options: So the real piece is welded with the right settings
quiz.explain: Scrap lets you dial in the settings before touching the real work.

days.title: Weld a Small Frame
days.goal: Weld four bars into a square frame.
steps: Cut four bars to size with a grinder or saw.
Tack the corners, check the frame is square.
Weld each corner fully.
Check the frame is flat and square.
days.task: Weld a square frame that is flat and true.
days.challenge: Weld a frame with all four corners square.

quiz.q: How do you cut the bars for a frame?
quiz.explain: Cut four bars to size with a grinder or saw.

quiz.q: What should you check after you tack the frame corners?
quiz.explain: Tack the corners, check the frame is square.

quiz.q: How do you finish a welded frame?
options: Check it is flat and square.
quiz.explain: Check the frame is flat and square.

days.title: Stick Welding Practice
days.goal: Practise stick welding until your beads are neat.
steps: Run beads on flat, then on a corner joint.
Practise starting and stopping cleanly.
Chip slag and look for holes (porosity) in your beads.
Repeat your weakest bead until it improves.
days.task: Run ten beads and keep your three best.
days.challenge: Run a bead with no holes in it at all.

quiz.q: Why practise beads on flat metal first?
options: Flat beads teach speed, angle and distance before joints
quiz.explain: Flat practice builds the hand control every joint needs.

quiz.q: What are holes in a weld called?
quiz.explain: Porosity is tiny holes from gas trapped in the weld, often from dirty metal.

quiz.q: What causes porosity in a weld?
quiz.explain: Rust, paint and damp rods trap gas in the weld and leave holes.

days.title: Project: Weld a Small Metal Frame
days.goal: Weld a small frame for a table or stool.
steps: Cut the bars to your plan.
Tack, check square, then weld fully.
Grind the welds smooth where hands will touch.
Test the frame: it should hold weight without bending.
days.task: Finish a small welded frame, square and strong.
days.challenge: Build a frame that holds your weight.

quiz.q: What should you do to the welds where hands will touch?
quiz.explain: Grind the welds smooth where hands will touch.

quiz.q: How do you test a welded frame?
options: It should hold weight without bending.
quiz.explain: Test the frame: it should hold weight without bending.

quiz.q: What is the right order for welding a frame?
options: Tack, check square, then weld fully.
quiz.explain: Tack, check square, then weld fully.

project.title: Weld a Small Metal Frame
project.brief: Weld a small frame for a table or stool, square and strong.

days.title: MIG Welding Basics
days.goal: Learn MIG welding: wire feed, gas and settings.
steps: MIG welding feeds a wire through a gun while gas shields the weld.
Learn the parts: the gun, the wire spool and the gas bottle.
Set the wire speed and voltage for your metal thickness.
Practise on scrap before the real piece.
days.task: Set up a MIG welder and run a bead on scrap.
days.challenge: Explain how MIG is different from stick welding.

quiz.q: How does MIG welding work?
options: A wire feeds through a gun while gas shields the weld.
quiz.explain: MIG welding feeds a wire through a gun while gas shields the weld.

quiz.q: What are the parts of a MIG welder?
options: The gun, the wire spool and the gas bottle.
quiz.explain: Learn the parts: the gun, the wire spool and the gas bottle.

quiz.q: What should you set on a MIG welder for your metal thickness?
quiz.explain: Set the wire speed and voltage for your metal thickness.

days.title: MIG Beads on Flat Metal
days.goal: Run neat MIG beads on flat metal.
steps: Hold the gun at a steady angle and distance.
Pull the trigger and move at a steady speed.
Listen for a steady crackle: that is the sound of a good MIG weld.
Check the bead is even with no holes.
days.task: Run five neat MIG beads on flat metal.
days.challenge: Run a MIG bead that sounds like steady bacon frying.

quiz.q: How does MIG welding work?
options: A wire feeds through a gun while gas shields the weld
quiz.explain: MIG feeds wire automatically and shields the weld with gas.

quiz.q: What sound does a good MIG weld make?
options: A steady crackle like bacon frying
quiz.explain: A steady crackle means the wire speed and voltage are right.

quiz.q: What does the gas do in MIG welding?
options: Shields the hot metal from air so the weld stays clean
quiz.explain: Shielding gas keeps air away so the weld does not fill with holes.

days.title: MIG Joints
days.goal: Weld butt and corner joints with MIG.
steps: Tack the pieces, check square, then weld.
Use short steady passes, not one long rush.
Let the weld cool between passes on thin metal.
Check the back of the joint for full penetration (the weld reaching through).
days.task: MIG weld a butt joint and a corner joint.
days.challenge: Weld a joint that holds when you bend it.

quiz.q: What should you do before you MIG weld a joint?
options: Tack the pieces and check square.
quiz.explain: Tack the pieces, check square, then weld.

quiz.q: How should you weld a MIG joint?
options: In short steady passes, not one long rush.
quiz.explain: Use short steady passes, not one long rush.

quiz.q: What should you check on the back of a MIG joint?
options: Full penetration, the weld reaching through.
quiz.explain: Check the back of the joint for full penetration (the weld reaching through).

days.title: MIG vs Stick: Which to Use
days.goal: Know when to use MIG and when to use stick.
steps: MIG is faster and cleaner on thin metal indoors.
Stick works outdoors in wind and on rusty metal.
MIG needs gas and a clean surface.
Choose the right process for each job.
days.task: Pick the right welding process for three different jobs.
days.challenge: Explain MIG vs stick to a friend in plain words.

quiz.q: When is MIG the better choice?
quiz.explain: MIG is faster and cleaner on thin metal indoors.

quiz.q: When is stick the better choice?
options: Outdoors in wind and on rusty metal.
quiz.explain: Stick works outdoors in wind and on rusty metal.

quiz.q: What does MIG need that stick does not?
quiz.explain: MIG needs gas and a clean surface.

days.title: Project: MIG Weld a Small Table Frame
days.goal: MIG weld a small table frame.
steps: Cut the bars to your plan.
Tack, check square, then MIG weld each joint.
Grind the welds smooth.
Test the frame for strength and squareness.
days.task: Finish a MIG-welded table frame, square and strong.
days.challenge: Build the frame with clean welds and no holes.

quiz.q: What should you do after you cut the bars for the table frame?
options: Tack, check square, then MIG weld each joint.
quiz.explain: Tack, check square, then MIG weld each joint.

quiz.q: What should you do to the MIG welds on the table frame?
quiz.explain: Grind the welds smooth.

quiz.q: What should you test on the finished table frame?
quiz.explain: Test the frame for strength and squareness.

days.title: Clean Metal Before Welding
days.goal: Clean metal so your welds are strong, not full of holes.
steps: Grind off rust, paint and dirt from the joint area.
Wipe the metal with a clean cloth.
Learn that dirty metal makes weak welds full of holes.
Clean both sides of every joint before you weld.
days.task: Clean a rusty piece until it shines, then weld it.
days.challenge: Tell a clean weld from a dirty one by looking.

quiz.q: What should you grind off the joint area before welding?
quiz.explain: Grind off rust, paint and dirt from the joint area.

quiz.q: What should you do after grinding the metal clean?
options: Wipe it with a clean cloth.
quiz.explain: Wipe the metal with a clean cloth.

quiz.q: Why does dirty metal make weak welds?
options: It makes welds full of holes.
quiz.explain: Dirty metal makes weak welds full of holes.

days.title: Grinding and Finishing Welds
days.goal: Grind welds smooth and safe to touch.
steps: Wear glasses and gloves when grinding.
Grind the high spots flat with a flap disc.
Round sharp edges so no one gets cut.
Check the finished weld is smooth and strong.
days.task: Grind a weld smooth without thinning the metal.
days.challenge: Finish a weld so it feels smooth to the touch.

quiz.q: What should you wear when you grind?
quiz.explain: Wear glasses and gloves when grinding.

quiz.q: What do you use to grind high spots flat?
quiz.explain: Grind the high spots flat with a flap disc.

quiz.q: Why round sharp edges after grinding?
quiz.explain: Round sharp edges so no one gets cut.

project.title: MIG Weld a Small Table Frame
project.brief: MIG weld a table frame, square, strong and clean.
checks: MIG welds neat with no holes

days.title: Cut Metal Safely
days.goal: Cut metal straight with a grinder or saw.
steps: Mark the cut line clearly.
Clamp the metal firmly before you cut.
Cut slowly and let the tool do the work.
File the cut edge smooth.
days.task: Cut four bars to exact lengths with clean ends.
days.challenge: Cut a bar square with less than 2mm of error.

quiz.q: What should you do before you cut metal?
options: Mark the cut line clearly and clamp the metal firmly.
quiz.explain: Mark the cut line clearly. Clamp the metal firmly before you cut.

quiz.q: How should you cut metal?
options: Slowly, letting the tool do the work.
quiz.explain: Cut slowly and let the tool do the work.

quiz.q: What should you do to a cut edge?
quiz.explain: File the cut edge smooth.

days.title: Build a Metal Gate Frame
days.goal: Plan and build a small metal gate frame.
steps: Measure the opening the gate must fit.
Draw the frame with its bars and diagonal brace.
Cut the bars and tack the frame square.
Weld fully and check it fits the opening.
days.task: Build a gate frame that fits its opening.
days.challenge: Build a gate frame that is square and does not sag.

quiz.q: What should you do first when you build a gate frame?
options: Measure the opening the gate must fit.
quiz.explain: Measure the opening the gate must fit.

quiz.q: What should you draw for the gate frame?
options: The frame with its bars and diagonal brace.
quiz.explain: Draw the frame with its bars and diagonal brace.

quiz.q: What should you check after you weld the gate frame?
quiz.explain: Weld fully and check it fits the opening.

days.title: Gate Hinges and Latches
days.goal: Fit hinges and a latch so a gate swings and shuts well.
steps: Weld hinge plates to the frame and the post.
Hang the gate and check it swings freely.
Fit a latch that clicks shut.
Adjust until the gate closes without lifting.
days.task: Fit hinges and a latch on a practice gate.
days.challenge: Hang a gate that swings and shuts first time.

quiz.q: Where do you weld hinge plates?
options: To the frame and the post.
quiz.explain: Weld hinge plates to the frame and the post.

quiz.q: What should you check after you hang the gate?
quiz.explain: Hang the gate and check it swings freely.

quiz.q: How should a good latch work?
quiz.explain: Fit a latch that clicks shut.

days.title: Steel Door Frames
days.goal: Weld a steel door frame square and strong.

video.title: How to Build a 15' Metal Property Gate

steps: Cut the frame pieces to size.
Tack the corners and check square with diagonals.
Weld fully and grind the corners smooth.
Test the frame with a door: it should fit with an even gap.
days.task: Weld a door frame that fits a door evenly.
days.challenge: Weld a frame with even gaps all round the door.

quiz.q: What should you do after you weld a door frame fully?
quiz.explain: Weld fully and grind the corners smooth.

quiz.q: How do you check a frame is square?
options: Measure both diagonals: equal means square
quiz.explain: Equal diagonals prove the frame is square.

quiz.q: Why tack before welding fully?
options: To hold parts in place and check square first
quiz.explain: Tacks hold the shape so you can check square before the full weld locks it.

days.title: Price a Welding Job
days.goal: Price a welding job from metal, time and a fair profit.

video.title: How to Build a 15' Metal Property Gate

steps: List the metal, rods, gas and discs the job needs.
Time the job and value your hours fairly.
Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean price.
Write a simple quote a customer can understand.
days.task: Write a clear quote for a small gate, parts and labour shown.
days.challenge: Price a table frame fairly.

quiz.q: What should you list first when you price a welding job?
options: The metal, rods, gas and discs the job needs.
quiz.explain: List the metal, rods, gas and discs the job needs.

quiz.q: How do you value your time on a job?
options: Time the job and value your hours fairly.
quiz.explain: Time the job and value your hours fairly.

quiz.q: How much profit should you add to a welding job?
quiz.explain: Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean price.

days.title: Hang a Metal Gate
days.goal: Hang a gate frame on hinges so it swings smoothly.

video.title: How to Build a 15' Metal Property Gate

steps: Check the frame is square before you hang it.
Fit hinges to the post first, then to the gate.
Hang the gate and check it swings without scraping.
Fit a latch that closes easily.
days.task: Hang a practice gate so it swings smoothly.
days.challenge: Hang a gate that does not sag.

quiz.q: What should you fit first when you hang a gate?
options: Hinges to the post, then to the gate.
quiz.explain: Fit hinges to the post first, then to the gate.

quiz.q: How do you check a frame is square?
options: Measure both diagonals: equal means square
quiz.explain: Equal diagonals prove the frame is square.

quiz.q: How should the gate close after you fit the latch?
quiz.explain: Fit a latch that closes easily.

days.title: Write a Welding Quote
days.goal: Write a clear quote for a welding job.

video.title: How to Weld Steel Door Frames

steps: List the metal, rods and discs you need and their cost.
Add your time at a fair hourly rate.
Add profit and write the total clearly.
Write what the quote covers so the customer understands.
days.task: Write a quote for a small gate frame.
days.challenge: Quote a job you have never done before.

quiz.q: What should a welding quote include?
options: Metal, rods, gas, discs, time and profit
quiz.explain: A real quote covers materials, time and profit.

quiz.q: What should your quote say it covers?
options: What the quote covers, so the customer understands.
quiz.explain: Write what the quote covers so the customer understands.

quiz.q: How should you write the total on a quote?
quiz.explain: Add profit and write the total clearly.

days.title: Capstone Planning
days.goal: Choose your capstone build, buy the metal and plan the day.

video.title: How to Weld Steel Door Frames

steps: Pick a gate, frame or furniture piece that shows your skills.
Buy or gather all metal, rods and discs.
Cut and label every piece in build order.
Write a two-day build plan with time for grinding and painting.
days.task: Have all capstone pieces cut and labelled, ready to weld.
days.challenge: Plan a capstone build that uses MIG or stick, grinding and paint.

quiz.q: What should your capstone build show?
quiz.explain: Pick a gate, frame or furniture piece that shows your skills.

quiz.q: What should you gather before capstone day?
quiz.explain: Buy or gather all metal, rods and discs.

quiz.q: What should your two-day build plan include?
quiz.explain: Write a two-day build plan with time for grinding and painting.

days.title: Capstone: Build and Present
days.goal: Build your capstone piece, finish it and present it.

video.title: How to Weld Steel Door Frames

steps: Weld the piece following your plan, checking it is square.
Grind smooth, paint or seal it.
Photograph it from four angles.
Present it with your costing sheet and care note.
days.task: Present a finished capstone piece with photos and costing.
days.challenge: Finish the piece with time left for paint to dry.

quiz.q: What should a welding quote include?
options: Metal, rods, gas, discs, time and profit
quiz.explain: A real quote covers materials, time and profit.

quiz.q: Why grind welds before painting?
options: So paint sticks to smooth clean metal
quiz.explain: Paint sticks best to clean smooth metal, not rough slag.

quiz.q: What should you present with your finished capstone piece?
options: Your costing sheet and care note.
quiz.explain: Present it with your costing sheet and care note.

capstone.title: Build a Metal Gate, Frame or Furniture Piece
capstone.brief: Design and build a metal gate, frame or furniture piece for a real home, welded, ground smooth and painted, and present it with a costing sheet.
checks: Welds ground smooth and safe to touch
Costing sheet shows metal, rods, gas, time and price
deliverables: Finished metal piece, strong and safe
Four photos: front, side, back and detail
